why_this_exists: The divergence counter in threeway.json counts distance FROM APPLE. It does not count DISTANCE FROM A DELIVERABLE, and that is the gap that let this project run for a day with 130 measurement files, 40 measuring tools and twelve evidence documents, and NOTHING ANYONE CAN OPEN IN KiCAD OR SEND TO A FABRICATOR. We had an instrument for one axis of drift and none for the other, so the Replica could move steadily away from being a buildable thing while every number about fidelity improved. THIS IS THE MISSING AXIS. It is red until KiCad can open something.
the_rule: A ROW IS GREEN ONLY WHEN A FILE EXISTS THAT THE RELEVANT TOOL CAN ACTUALLY OPEN. A path that exists is not an artifact. Every row therefore carries a FORMAT PROBE - a string the real format must contain - and an empty file, a stub, or a file of the wrong kind at the right name all stay RED. The selftest watches each of those three cases fail on purpose, because a check that only ever goes red proves nothing about its own ability to go green.
anti_gaming: The board and schematic rows additionally REFUSE a file whose sha256 matches halo_rev_a's equivalent. The cheapest way to turn this check green without doing the work is to copy the board Leif rejected into the Replica's tree, and that would be the exact failure this check exists to catch, dressed as a pass.
search: Each row GLOBS the whole Replica tree for its extension rather than demanding one guessed path. The design lanes choose their own layout; this check asks whether an artifact of the right KIND exists and opens, not whether it sits where L9 imagined it would.

rows.probe_is: the s-expression header KiCad's schematic editor requires
rows.why_it_is_required: There is no circuit until there is a schematic. Every net, every part and every connection the Replica claims to copy from Apple lives here or lives nowhere.
rows.timestamp_note: ROOT ARTIFACT - a schematic has no upstream file in this graph, so freshness is not applicable. Its own mtime is the source for D2, D4 and D5.

rows.why_it_is_required: The netlist is the schematic in the form the board tool consumes. Without it a board file is a drawing of copper rather than a realisation of a circuit, and nothing can check that the copper matches the schematic.
rows.timestamp_note: KiCad writes (date "...") into the netlist. EMBEDDED, strong. Its source D1 has no embedded stamp, so this comparison is EMBEDDED vs MTIME.

rows.probe_is: the s-expression header of a KiCad footprint
rows.why_it_is_required: Apple's parts are WLCSP-50, WLCSP-10, 0201 and a wound coil. None of those has a stock footprint that fits this board, and the Replica's whole claim is that its geometry is measured rather than assumed. The measured geometry has to become land patterns or it is not in the design.
rows.timestamp_note: ROOT ARTIFACT. Footprints are authored, not derived. Their mtime is a source for D4.

rows.why_it_is_required: THIS IS THE ONE LEIF ASKED FOR. His words were 'the exact pcb design and all the components'. Until this row is green there is no PCB design, only an apparatus for measuring one.
rows.timestamp_note: A .kicad_pcb carries no creation timestamp, so mtime is all there is. WEAK on both sides. The board must postdate BOTH the schematic and the footprint library - a board rebuilt before a footprint was edited is stale even though nothing about it looks wrong.

precondition.why: A board built from a schematic that never passed ERC inherits the schematic's faults in copper, where they cost a fabrication run to find.

rows.probe_is: the KiCad ERC report's own $schema URL. It was the bare substring 'erc', which matches any JSON whose name or body happens to contain those three letters.
rows.why_it_is_required: A schematic nobody ran the rule checker over is a claim, not a verified circuit. This project's own standard is that a check which never ran is verification debt.
rows.timestamp_note: KiCad's ERC report carries its own run date. EMBEDDED, strong, against D1's mtime.

rows.probe_is: the KiCad DRC report's own $schema URL. IT WAS THE BARE SUBSTRING 'drc', which admitted drc-liveness.json and drc-liveness-per-item.json - files that are not DRC reports at all - and summing their contents produced a verdict of 1016 errors that belonged to no board.
rows.why_it_is_required: Same argument one level down, and it is the row THREE-WAY.md row 23 turns on: halo_rev_a is a design that CAN be wrong and is measured to be wrong in four height rows. The Replica cannot be wrong in that sense at all, because there is nothing to check.
rows.timestamp_note: KiCad's DRC report carries its own run date. EMBEDDED, strong, against D4's mtime. A DRC older than the board it grades is the most dangerous stale artifact here, because it reports PASS on copper it never saw.

precondition.why: A DRC on a board whose schematic never passed ERC grades the copper against a netlist that may itself be wrong.

rows.probe_is: the RS-274X extended-attribute header every KiCad gerber layer opens with
rows.why_it_is_required: A board file is what WE can open. Gerbers are what a FABRICATOR can open. Nothing gets made without them.
rows.rev_a_note: halo_rev_a HAS NOT GOT THESE EITHER. This row is red for both boards, and saying so is the point - a check that only accuses the Replica would be measuring the wrong thing.
rows.timestamp_note: Gerbers carry %TF.CreationDate. EMBEDDED, strong, against D4's mtime. GLOB CORRECTED 2026-09-05: it was **/*.gbr, which catches only the DRILL MAPS - a real KiCad gerber set is .gtl .gbl .g1 .g2 .gts .gbs .gto .gbo .gm1, none of which end in .gbr. The old glob would have called a set complete while seeing none of its copper layers.

precondition.why: A fabrication set cut from a board with unrouted nets is FRESH AND UNBUILDABLE. It passes existence and it passes freshness, and it is a WORSE artifact than a stale one precisely because both of the other assertions wave it through. halo-cb is deliberately NOT regenerating rev_a's gerbers for this reason - the board still has 28 unconnected nets - and that refusal is what exposed the third leg.

rows.probe_is: the header of an Excellon drill program
rows.why_it_is_required: The board is annular with a routed centre pocket and three plated tooling holes. Every one of those is a drill or route operation and none of them exists until this file does.
rows.rev_a_note: halo_rev_a HAS NOT GOT THIS EITHER. Red for both.
rows.timestamp_note: Excellon files carry the same TF.CreationDate comment. EMBEDDED, strong, against D4's mtime.

precondition.why: A fabrication set cut from a board with unrouted nets is FRESH AND UNBUILDABLE. It passes existence and it passes freshness, and it is a WORSE artifact than a stale one precisely because both of the other assertions wave it through. halo-cb is deliberately NOT regenerating rev_a's gerbers for this reason - the board still has 28 unconnected nets - and that refusal is what exposed the third leg.

freshness.why: AN ARTIFACT THAT OPENS IS NOT AN ARTIFACT THAT IS CURRENT. halo_rev_a's gerbers open perfectly and describe a board that no longer exists: they carry an embedded KiCad creation date of 2026-09-05T06:06:39 while the board file they came from has an mtime of 07:54:19 - 6,460 seconds later, an hour and three quarters in which the board gained the NFC coil keep-out, lost plane copper under the coil, and was rerouted from 83 unconnected items to 28. A pure existence test reads that GREEN. EXISTENCE IS ADJACENT TO CURRENCY, which is the same failure shape as every other control this lane broke today.
freshness.the_rule: Every non-root artifact must be NEWER THAN EVERY ONE OF ITS SOURCES. A set of files is only as fresh as its OLDEST member; a source is as new as its NEWEST member. Both directions are the conservative one.
freshness.three_states: FRESH -> the row can be green. STALE -> RED. SOURCE ABSENT -> CANNOT DETERMINE, never green and never red: an artifact with no source to compare against is UNMEASURED, not stale, and this project does not let an unmeasured thing occupy the same field as a measured one.
freshness.timestamp_strength: An EMBEDDED timestamp - one the generating tool wrote into its own output - is preferred wherever it exists. mtime is the fallback and it is WEAK: a git checkout rewrites every mtime to checkout time, which can make a stale artifact look fresh or a fresh one look stale. Every row records which kind it used, and a comparison that mixes an embedded stamp against an mtime says so.

rev_a.label: halo_rev_a
rev_a.note: rev_a's artifacts are spread across three roots - the board and schematic under electronics/halo_rev_a, the fabrication set under out/release/board/gerber, the checks under out/verify. Searching only the first is what led this lane to report, wrongly, that rev_a had no gerbers. IT HAS TWELVE. The conclusion survived for a different and worse reason: they are stale.

validity.why: THE THIRD LEG, and it is the same shape a third time. EXISTENCE IS ADJACENT TO CURRENCY, AND CURRENCY IS ADJACENT TO VALIDITY. Each assertion is satisfied by something NEXT TO what we actually want, and each one alone reads as evidence. Three legs is not belt-and-braces - they are three genuinely different properties one artifact can independently fail: it can be absent, it can be stale, and it can be a faithful cut of a board that was never fit to cut.
validity.the_rule: An artifact's SOURCE must have PASSED ITS OWN CHECKS. A gerber's precondition is the board's DRC verdict; a board's and a DRC's precondition is the schematic's ERC verdict. If that verdict is ABSENT rather than failing, the row is CANNOT DETERMINE and not green - an unrun check is not a passed one.
validity.counted_how: KiCad reports carry severities. Only severity 'error' counts against the verdict; warnings are reported and do not block. Unconnected items are counted separately and DO block a fabrication set, because an unrouted net is not a warning about a board, it is a board that does not work.

callable_by_other_repos: halo-cb: 'a check I have to be told about is one I will eventually not be told about.' So this is an instrument, not a section of our report: `k_threeway deliverable --roots <path> [<path> ...]` runs the same three legs against any tree a caller names, exits 0/1/2, and needs nothing from this lane.

the_fourth_column.why: A REPORT'S ROW STATE AND A REPORT'S CONTENTS ARE DIFFERENT FACTS, and with only three columns the first reads as the second. D6 showed valid=yes, which by this file's own rules means ITS SOURCE (the ERC) was clean - and reads to anyone scanning a table for green as 'the DRC passed'. It did not: the Replica's DRC reports 42 errors against 3 warnings, with actual clearances down to 0.0000 mm. The column that says so is now beside it. Documenting the trap was the weaker option; removing it is this one.
the_fourth_column.what_a_report_row_being_GREEN_means: the report EXISTS, OPENS, is NEWER than the thing it grades, and came from a source that had itself passed. It says NOTHING about what the report FOUND. A DRC listing 42 errors is a perfectly good ARTIFACT and a perfectly bad BOARD - different objects, and this table now shows both.
the_fourth_column.why_a_failing_report_does_not_turn_its_o: the artifact is not the defect. Turning D6 red on its contents would conflate 'we have no DRC' with 'the DRC found things', and this project already has a standing rule against conflating could-not-build with could-not-verify. Contents become a GATE where something DEPENDS on them - which is exactly what the third leg does for D7 and D8.
the_fourth_column.columns: opens | current | source ok | ITS OWN VERDICT. The third column was labelled 'valid', which is the word that invited the misreading; it is now 'source ok'.
the_fourth_column.notation: nE = errors, nU = unconnected items. Warnings are reported in the row detail and do not gate.
